newsitem.title: USA: Wheelabrator says defers Dutch auction plan.
newsitem.headline: Wheelabrator says defers Dutch auction plan.

text.p: Wheelabrator Technologies Inc said it deferred indefinitely a previously announced plan to hold a Dutch auction tender offer for its own shares.

In January, the company's board authorized a 30-million share repurchase program, including a $350-million Dutch auction anticipated to take place in the second quarter of this year, the company said.
The Dutch auction is being deferred to give management "additional flexibility to assess investment opportunities in Wheelabrator's core business," the company said.
Chief executive John Kehoe said, "At the same time, the company currently has the ability to continue to buy back its shares as and when the circumstances warrant."
Wheelabrator is a majority-owned subsidiary of Oak Brook, Ill.-based WMX Technologies Inc, which is engaged in a massive restructuring under pressure from dissatisfied shareholders.
